comments: CHI is sorting objects in response to MOT's question 'für wen is(t) das?'; 'das nicht' denies the assignment of the object.
The token 'alle' in 'alle raus' is used as a quantifier meaning 'all/everything' rather than the negation meaning 'all gone/empty'.
Child corrects mother's question (line 4950) about driving the stroller by specifying the presence of bunnies in the stroller.
Child says 'nein da' (not there) while arranging figures, vetoing the current placement/state after MOT says 'prima'.
Child rejects the mother's proposed way of lying down ('noch mal so?') to replace it with another.
Child vetoes the location for picking up the stool ('nicht hier ab') during a negotiation about seating.
Child asserts that an object is gone/absent, confirmed by Mother's follow-up 'is(t) weg?'
Child corrects the adult's statement about who is present/being shown the object ("das ist ja gar nicht deine Mama" -> "ne Opa Ernst zeig(e)n").
Child is in a struggle over a toy (the Flipper) with Thorsten; 'ne' blocks Thorsten's claim to the toy by asserting he already has it.
Child resists Opa's prompts to take the toy or come closer (lines 126717, 126723).
Child denies the mother's question 'is der für n Papi?' by asserting the money is theirs ('mein deld').
Child denies the truth of the factual question 'kriegen wir das jetz(t), das Geld?'
Child rejects the proposal/directive to move over (line 217357).
Child answers a question about their desire to continue painting (line 240927); this is a claim about a state of affairs.
Child denies the mother's assertion in line 250007 that she has poop in her pants.
Child states that something does not fit; negated fit is a claim about the world, which is coded as Denial.
Child states that a figure does not fit into the car ('geht nicht rein'), which is a claim about fit/success.
Child refuses to put on shoes in the context of a discussion about buying new ones; MOT responds with 'doch' (insistence).
Child answers Mother's question "is(t) da ein Spiegel?" by asserting the mirror is absent.
Child claims the toy phone is broken and doesn't turn on; this is a factual claim about the world.
Child contests the adult's claim that it is 'schon fertig' (line 281157) by asking 'nicht noch mehr?'
Child remarks that the lid is gone/absent, following the mother's statement in line 281766.
Child contradicts mother's assertion in line 282477 that the animal is just born.
Child states a normative rule that the dog should not have the ball; the subsequent exchange with the mother confirms it as a rule statement rather than a move to stop the dog.
Child makes a factual claim about the mouse's inability to eat the snail; no offer or directive is being refused.
Child states they do not know the animal in response to the mother's question; a factual claim about knowledge.
The token 'alle' is used as a quantifier meaning 'all of them' (confirmed by GIS: 'du willst alles haben?'), not as a negation meaning 'all gone'.
Child reports a failure of fit/action ('that doesn't work'), which is a claim about the world.
Child is commenting on the physical fit of an object; negated fit is a claim about the world.
Child rejects the object/task he was struggling with (line 283509), moving on to another toy in the next turn.
Child denies the mother's assertion about the child's desire to play more (line 283525); fits Trap 1 (assertion about speaker).
Child expresses not wanting a specific object ('das') during play, which functions as a rejection/veto of that object.
Child refuses to continue the activity of building, confirmed by mother's follow-up 'what do you want to do then?'
Child answers mother's question about what they want to do by stating they want to do nothing; second occurrence is a repetition.
Child refuses the mother's directive to tidy up ('einräum(e)n'), confirmed by subsequent 'ich will noch weiter machen'.
Child reports that something 'doesn't work' while tidying up; negated success is a claim about the world.
Child reports that a physical action with the toy is not working; a claim about the world.
The negation is immediately followed by 'hier sind keiner da' (no one is here), indicating the child is remarking on the absence of the person on the phone.
Child remarks that the container is empty; Mother confirms with 'alles leer, ne, Sina?', indicating Nonexistence.
Child refuses the mother's request to tidy up ('räums(t) du bitte mal auf?').
Child vetoes the mother's implied placement of a piece and proposes an alternative location ('der soll da dran').
Child denies the caregiver's claim that she is also a sheep (line 360230), clarified by her subsequent identity statement.
